title: Savior out of the Blue
subtitle: She saved a potential embarrassment and salvaged a heart that couldn't let go.

items.text: Savior out of the Blue

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: The war came, forcing all of us to put aside childish things and grow up—myself included.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It was a cruel and solemn mass farewell.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It forced every one of us to say goodbye to our dreams, to the past, and to the world we knew.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Before I knew it, I was conscripted and boarded an army jeep, venturing into foreign lands.
1940s, Officers' Club

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Before I knew it, I was conscripted and boarded an army jeep, venturing into foreign lands.
The atmosphere rises amidst the clinking of glasses, as if everyone should toast to the victory at hand ...
... while they still can.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Cheers, gents!
He drains his glass in one gulp.

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: To a brighter tomorrow!

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: Sergeant Finn, why the hell are ya still clutching that little book of yours? You ain't writing sweet nothings to a dame back home, are ya?!

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Come on, there's nothing wrong with that! And I can tell you now, Pete, when you get back home, you'll be spinning tales even taller than Brian here!

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Go ahead and write whatever you want, Brian, and don't forget to mention the part where I led the charge.
He slaps Brian's shoulder heartily. Brian clutches his notebook.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: This isn't a letter; it's my research.

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: Oh, now that's something ya don't hear every day! Lemme have a look!
He strides forward, snatching the notebook from Brian's hands.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Hey! They're just a few rough ideas! It's not finished yet!
The other man doesn't seem to care.

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: "A compilation of data on mysterious vampires ..."

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: Haha, you ain't got a torch for our Miss Julia, have ya?

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: I'll admit, she's got a gentle touch when she's bandaging us up, and the way she draws blood is very light! I almost fell asleep the last time she did it.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Tough luck, Brian. You've got more rivals here than a dog has fleas.

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: But I'm sure comparing Miss Julia to a vampire would earn you a sock on the jaw from some of the straighter shooters in this squad.
They look at Brian with pity, as if mourning this lost cause.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: This isn't for Julia.
Brian shakes his head firmly, a serious expression on his face.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Being called a vampire is hardly insulting! They're symbols of beauty, purity, and everlasting life.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Haha, you say that, but have you ever even laid eyes on a real vampire?

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: They're just made-up stories I believed when I was a kid.

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: But I'll grant ya that they're pretty handy for spooking the little rascals!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I've seen a real vampire.
They fall into a brief silence.
Then, a burst of raucous laughter.

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: I gotta hand it to ya, Sergeant Finn; your sense of humor's something else. You've got a real knack for story-telling!

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I'm being serious. When I was a kid, I saw her.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ever since then, I've been on the hunt for more information about her, even just the slightest sliver.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: She was perfect. Everything I could ever imagine. Just like—

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Haha, what are you looking at?

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: Brian, ya don't think there's a vampire lurking somewhere at this shindig, do ya?
Brian scans the room, eagerly seeking to validate his claim.
The club is bustling with people. The heavy conversation and crisscrossing lights make his head spin.
As Brian's eyes sweep the room, he abruptly comes to a halt.
What a delight it is to see you here again, Mrs. Kate.

items.speaker: Kate
items.text: Isn't it just? It's been ages since we last saw each other!

items.speaker: Kate
items.text: Oh, how I envy you, Winnifred. You haven't aged a bit!

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Heh. Time does have an elusive magic, doesn't it?
Brian's hands begin to tremble. He rubs his eyes in disbelief.
He tries to speak, but the lump in his throat says otherwise. Then he croaks out.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: It's her ...
Before he realizes what he's doing, he's striding toward her.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Hey, Brian, what's the big idea?
He tugs at Brian's sleeve, his voice lowered.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: Have you lost it, man?! I know she's a looker—even more so than Miss Julia—but that lady's way out of our league.

items.speaker: Officer I
items.text: I spied her over in the commander's office. Even the top brass tip their hats to her.

items.speaker: Officer II
items.text: I hear she's a special guest of our munitions supplier. Even got ties to the underground here, apparently. Ya better kiss that pipe dream goodbye.
He grabs the air where the cuff of Brian's shirt should be, but it is already gone.
Brian is now standing in front of her, the notebook in his hand trembling violently.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ahem. Hello ... ma'am.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Hmm ...?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Hello, sir. That was quite the entrance.
She smiles gently, seemingly used to such disturbances.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Oh, please accept my apologies, ma'am. I didn't mean to offend you; it's just ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: You look just like someone I met a long time ago.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Heh ... Not exactly the slickest line I've ever heard.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Sir, if you hope to make new acquaintances, I sincerely suggest you choose a less clichéd opener next time.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I'm gathering information on vampires. That's why I had to talk to you.
The lady before him chuckles ambiguously.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: You catch on quick.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: But do I really look like a vampire? Perhaps it's because of my striking white hair?

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: It is saddening when those noble ladies pester me to reveal the secret behind maintaining such a style.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: No, no, you misunderstand.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: I believe that vampires are a special race possessing advantages ordinary people don't.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: For instance, using human blood as nourishment allows them to gain stronger physiques and, more importantly, maintain their vitality and appearance for much longer.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: They're the embodiment of beauty and the favored children of God.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: That's quite an imaginative theory.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: But it doesn't quite align with medical science, does it?
She downs her drink in one swig.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: The creatures that most closely resemble your description are bats. They feed on human blood and are active at night, but they don't gain long lives or beautiful faces in doing so.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: On the contrary, they're filthy and germ-ridden, making them one of the animals we despise most. Even in the realm of arcane biology, no such individuals exist.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: If there is, in fact, a race capable of eternal life, they would be marred by ugliness and prone to disease.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: I, on the other hand, have heard some more substantial tales.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: The Rusalki by the water's edge.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: They have long flowing hair, snatch up sailors, and plunder their ships to maintain their appearance. Of course, rather than indulging in hearsay, you could always venture north and see them for yourself.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: But I swear, I've seen you before.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Hush!

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: If you don't want to be seen as an agent of the underworld or a spy dispatched by an arms dealer, stop attracting so much attention.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Those people are all ruthless extremists. They don't want anyone more than necessary to be mixed up in emerging intelligence.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: It'd be better for the both of us.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Thank you.
Brian looks around. His companions are still waving at him from afar.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Nevertheless, I still believe that vampires exist. I won't give up.
He nods and makes to leave.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Wait ... young man ...
It's an exquisitely crafted business card, with both deep and shallow patterns reflected on it. It feels almost watery to the touch.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Take it.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Winnifred ... ma'am ... My name's Brian!

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Very good, Mr. Brian.

items.speaker: Winnifred
items.text: Maybe one day we'll do business together.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Ah ... Right.
Brian, momentarily stunned, realizes that she has already vanished without a trace.
He places the business card into his breast pocket, carefully smoothing out the creases.

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Brian
items.text: Did I really remember it all wrong?
TO BE CONTINUED…
